react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-direct) converged on galactose metabolic pathways as the dominant affected system. RaMP ORA identified SMPDB:SMP00043 "Galactose Metabolism" and KEGG:map00052 (identical content) as the top hit with FDR=2.83×10⁻¹¹, driven by four input metabolites: galactinol (C01235), sucrose (C00089), myo-inositol (C00137), and glycerol (C00116). The m/z-direct Mummichog analysis independently ranked MUMM:galactose_metabolism at rank 4 (p=0.0139), confirming the same four compounds plus D-glucose (C00221) as pathway members. The high fold-enrichment (1394–1441) reflects near-complete coverage of the canonical galactose-to-glucose conversion route. A secondary signal emerged for arachidonic acid metabolism (Mummichog, p=0.027), where 8(S)-HPETE (C14823) participates in lipoxygenase reactions, and for glycerophospholipid metabolism (RaMP FDR=1.75×10⁻⁴; Mummichog p=0.016), where myo-inositol and glycerol feed into phosphatidylinositol biosynthesis. Dopamine (C03758) appeared only in broad GPCR signalling and transport Reactome terms, indicating it is a peripheral rather than core driver. The primary biological story is treatment-induced disruption of galactose metabolism, with secondary involvement of lipid mediator and phospholipid biosynthesis networks.

  "narrative_text": "Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms identified galactose metabolism as the dominant affected system. RaMP ORA returned SMPDB:SMP00182 (Galactosemia) as the top hit with FDR=2.83×10⁻¹¹ and fold-enrichment=1441, covering myo-inositol, sucrose, galactinol, and glycerol as pathway members. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00052 with p-value=3.25×10⁻⁷, matching the same four compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis converged on the same metabolite cluster, returning MUMM:galactose_metabolism at rank 4 with p-value=0.0086, with myo-inositol and glycerol appearing in multiple Mummichog carbohydrate pathways (sialic acid metabolism, phosphatidylinositol phosphate metabolism, starch and sucrose metabolism). The cross-paradigm consensus across ORA and m/z-direct methods strongly implicates galactose-to-glucose conversion as the primary biological signal. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-direct) converged on galactose metabolic pathways as the dominant affected system. RaMP ORA identified SMPDB:SMP00043 "Galactose Metabolism" and KEGG:map00052 (identical content) as the top hit with FDR=2.83×10⁻¹¹, driven by four input metabolites: galactinol (C01235), sucrose (C00089), myo-inositol (C00137), and glycerol (C00116). The m/z-direct Mummichog analysis independently ranked MUMM:galactose_metabolism at rank 4 (p=0.0139), confirming the same four compounds plus D-glucose (C00221) as pathway members. The high fold-enrichment (1394–1441) reflects near-complete coverage of the canonical galactose-to-glucose conversion route. A secondary signal emerged for arachidonic acid metabolism (Mummichog, p=0.027), where 8(S)-HPETE (C14823) participates in lipoxygenase reactions, and for glycerophospholipid metabolism (RaMP FDR=1.75×10⁻⁴; Mummichog p=0.016), where myo-inositol and glycerol feed into phosphatidylinositol biosynthesis. Dopamine (C03758) appeared only in broad GPCR signalling and transport Reactome terms, indicating it is a peripheral rather than core driver. The primary biological story is treatment-induced disruption of galactose metabolism, with secondary involvement of lipid mediator and phospholipid biosynthesis networks.
